subject: AtlasPayments — encryption handoff, residency & logging ownership
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasPayments — post-demo encryption clarifications and next steps

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to capture the open items around encryption, residency and logging so we have a clear handoff for both engineering and procurement. I've summarized below and proposed owners/ETA.

Quick recap of your priorities (from the call):
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) for model input/output at-rest encryption
- KMS integration that supports key rotation and HSM-backed keys for a subset of workloads
- Data residency: all PII-derived artifacts must stay in us-east-1
- Audit logs for inference requests with 12-month retention, accessible to your security team

Open items & suggested owners: 
1) BYOK feasibility and supported key providers — Owner: Aditya (P0) — deliverable: short runbook comparing AWS KMS (CloudHSM), Azure Key Vault HSM, and on-prem HSM. ETA: Tue 24 Nov.
2) In-transit vs at-rest control mapping — Owner: Ben — deliverable: mapping doc with TLS profile, mutual-TLS options, and where envelope encryption is applied. ETA: Wed 25 Nov.
3) Logging/access model — Owner: Monica (me) — deliverable: proposed log retention/SCIM access pattern for Audit exports + sample retention SLA language for procurement. ETA: Thu 26 Nov.
4) Contract redlines re: key custody & telemetry — "Contracts Team" (you) + Redwood legal. I'll loop our contracts lead once we have the attached playbook notes you can review.

Attachments: KMS-options-summary.pdf (short comparison), redwood-encryption-playbook.docx (ops playbook snippet).

Next steps: If that looks right, can you confirm: (a) the set of workloads you want HSM-backed keys for (payments tokenization only?), and (b) whether you require keys to be managed in your AWS account or if a Redwood-managed HSM under a BYOK contract is acceptable.

Thanks — I can set up a 30-minute follow-up with Aditya and Ben early next week to walk the runbook.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
www.redwood.com

[Attachment: KMS-options-summary.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: redwood-encryption-playbook.docx (DOCX)]

From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlaspayments.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@atlaspayments.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPayments — post-demo encryption clarifications and next steps

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) HSM scope: initially payments tokenization (envs: prod and prod-DR). We may expand to token orchestration later, but tokenization is mission-critical.
2) Key ownership: preference is to keep keys in our AWS account (we run GovCloud workloads today). If we can use AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys and Redwood can integrate via IAM cross-account, that would be ideal.
3) Logging: the security team wants access to per-request metadata (request id, model id, vhost, timestamp, redacted input hash) and the ability to export logs to our S3 bucket every 24h with server-side encryption. Retention 12 months is fine.

I'll review the attached playbook and confirm by EOD Tue 24 Nov on whether we need a DPA amendment. Can you also include a brief section on key rotation automation (who triggers rotation, downtime expectations)?

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Engineering
AtlasPayments

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AtlasPayments — BYOK feasibility notes

Folks — I ran a quick pass on BYOK options and sketched the runbook. Key points: 

- AWS KMS w/ CloudHSM: supported; can do cross-account key usage via Grants + IAM role. Pros: simplest for Atlas since they want keys in their AWS account. Cons: no physical HSM separation from other tenants (but CloudHSM provides FIPS 140-2 level).
- Azure Key Vault HSM: feasible but adds complexity to cross-cloud networking; not our recommended path unless Atlas requires Azure.
- Customer HSM (on-prem) via PKCS#11: supported with extra network/topology work; adds latency and operational runbook.

Rotation: we support automated rotation flows via our key-wrapping service. We recommend a staged rotation: pre-rotate wrapped keys, test on canary model variants, then switch traffic. Downtime is avoidable if KV cache invalidation is handled carefully — I left detail in the attached runbook.

I'll attach the runbook excerpt to this thread. Ben, tagging you for the TLS/in-transit mapping.

- Aditya

[Attachment: kms-runbook-excerpt.md (MD)]

Subject: Re: AtlasPayments — encryption handoff, residency & logging ownership (next steps)

Sam — thanks for the confirmation and the scope callouts. Short update and concrete asks: 

- Aditya attached a runbook excerpt (see above). Action for Atlas: confirm whether the keys must live in GovCloud or standard AWS account. If GovCloud, we should set a call with infra to confirm network constraints.
- Ben to follow up with a one-page TLS + envelope-diagram (will include mutual TLS and client certs for admin APIs).
- On logs: we can deliver per-request metadata to your S3 via our secure delivery pipeline. We will redact PII prior to export by default but will include deterministic hashes for traceability. Action: please confirm the S3 bucket name and whether you require SSE-KMS with your key.

Procurement ask: Contracts, please expect a short amendment about BYOK responsibilities and key-rotation SLAs. Marissa is looped for commercial terms — she will propose language if Atlas confirms technical constraints.

Proposed next meeting: Thu 26 Nov 09:00 PT — 30 minutes to review runbook + TLS doc + contracts ask. I can send a calendar invite once Sam confirms.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
